title: Iran FA Chief Taj: FIFA Must Guarantee US Will Not 'Insult' IRGC Before Iran Travels to World Cup
detail: Iran Football Federation president Mehdi Taj issued a new political condition for Iran's World Cup participation on May 6: FIFA must provide official guarantees that the United States will not insult the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). 'Our host is FIFA, not Mr. Trump or America,' Taj stated. The demand follows the incident on April 29 where Taj himself was denied entry to Canada at Toronto Pearson Airport due to alleged IRGC ties, forcing him to miss the 76th FIFA Congress in Vancouver. Taj confirmed he will meet FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Zurich later in May to press for these guarantees. The condition creates a near-impossible diplomatic hurdle: the US officially designates the IRGC as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, making any formal commitment to 'not insult' it politically untenable under US law. Iran's Group G matches remain scheduled at US venues: SoFi Stadium (LA) on June 15 vs New Zealand and June 21 vs Belgium; Lumen Field (Seattle) on June 26 vs Egypt. The June 1 final squad submission deadline is 26 days away. Iran's provisional squad list is due to FIFA by May 11.

media.caption: Iran FA chief Taj demands FIFA guarantee the US will not insult the IRGC — meeting with Infantino in Zurich planned as June 1 squad deadline looms

title: FIFA Extends Prestianni Ban to World Cup — Argentina Winger Could Miss First Two Group Matches
detail: FIFA's Disciplinary Committee ruled on May 6 that the six-game UEFA ban imposed on Argentina winger Gianluca Prestianni (Benfica, 20) will be extended to have worldwide effect — ruling him out of Argentina's first two World Cup group matches if selected. The ban stems from a February 17, 2026 UEFA Champions League match where Prestianni admitted to using a homophobic slur directed at Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid. FIFA's extension makes the ban applicable to all FIFA-sanctioned competitions, not just European matches. If selected by coach Lionel Scaloni in the final 26-man squad (due June 1), Prestianni would miss Argentina's Group J openers vs. Algeria (June 17) and vs. Austria (June 21) at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, potentially returning for the third group match vs. Jordan (June 25). Argentina are the defending World Cup champions and are expected to include Prestianni in their preliminary squad (due May 11) pending appeal.

media.caption: FIFA extends Prestianni's ban globally — Argentina winger could miss first two World Cup group matches vs Algeria and Austria in Kansas City
